title: Shopping Cart
statement:
Tony is visiting a supermarket to buy Z cans of coke. The supermarket offers only two types of packs:

- A pack of 2 cans costs X dollars.
- A pack of 4 cans costs Y dollars.

Tony can purchase any number of these packs. He is allowed to buy more than Z cans if necessary, but he cannot buy individual cans.

For each test case, determine the minimum total cost required to purchase at least Z cans.

examples.explanation: Five 2-packs → 10 cans → Cost = 25. Two 4-packs + One 2-pack → Cost = 25. Minimum cost = 25.
Two 4-packs + One 2-pack → 10 cans → Cost = 21 (cheaper than five 2-packs at 25). Minimum cost = 21.
One 4-pack + One 2-pack → 6 cans → Cost = 11 (cheaper than three 2-packs at 12). Minimum cost = 11.

hints: Check if buying 4-packs is cheaper per can than buying 2-packs (i.e. Y < 2 * X).
If Y >= 2 * X, buy ceil(Z / 2) two-packs.
If Y < 2 * X, buy Z // 4 four-packs and resolve remainder cans efficiently.
discussion: Compare the cost of full 4-packs and optimal combinations for remaining cans.
